lines: There are people you meet…
And there are people you grow up with.
You were one of mine.
And somehow… more than 10 years later, I still remember us.
Today is your birthday.
So I made something for you.

childhood.title: Once Upon a Childhood
paragraphs: Before adulthood. Before distance. Before everybody got busy.
There was school, random conversations, laughing at things that were not really that funny, and being together without needing a reason.
The details below are deliberately yours to fill with the memories only you can actually remember.

thenNow.leftText: We were children when we knew each other best.
thenNow.rightText: I don't know every chapter you've lived since then. And that's okay. I just hope life has been kind to you — and that the girl I knew is still somewhere in the woman you've become.

question.prompt: What do you miss most about childhood?

branch.title: Maybe that's what growing up does to us.
lines: It doesn't always make us forget people.
Sometimes it simply makes us realise how much of our lives was shared with them.

branch.title: Honestly…
lines: We probably had no idea how good we had it.
Children are remarkably talented at turning ordinary days into stories.

branch.title: Funny how that works.
lines: The things we wanted to escape from as children can become the exact things we miss as adults.
Simple is a luxury we only recognise after it is gone.

branch.title: Exactly.
lines: The moments that become memories usually don't announce themselves first.
They are just ordinary moments that somehow survive.

letter.title: A Letter Across Time
paragraphs: I know this is probably not the kind of birthday message you expected from me.
It's actually funny thinking about how long it's been.
We were kids once. We were just there, living those little everyday moments without knowing that one day we'd look back at them and realise they were some of the good years.
Then life happened. Somehow more than ten years went by.
And even though we're far from the people we were back then, I've never forgotten that you were once a really important part of my life.
Some friendships don't need to remain exactly the same to still have meant something. Ours is one of those.
So today, I didn't just want to say happy birthday. I wanted to remind you that somewhere in your past, there is a little version of you who had a friend who genuinely loved having you around.
That friend is still here. Just older. Probably more tired. Hopefully wiser.
I hope this next chapter of your life is beautiful. I hope you find people who make life lighter. I hope you experience things that your younger self could not even imagine.
And I hope when you look back years from now, you'll realise you've lived a life worth remembering.
From one childhood friend to another, I'm glad our paths crossed.
